common.tagline: Organized Prayer for Those in Need

home.metadataTitle: PrayerTrain — Organized Prayer for Those in Need
home.heroBody: When someone you love is struggling, rally your parish and community to provide continuous prayer coverage. Create a prayer train, choose prayers, and invite others to sign up for specific days.
home.heroLogoAlt: PrayerTrain — a community united in prayer
home.howItWorksBody: Three simple steps to surround someone in organized, continuous prayer.
home.step1Body: Tell us about the person and their situation. We'll suggest appropriate prayers and generate a calendar of prayer slots.
home.step2Body: Send the link to your parish, prayer group, family, and friends. They pick specific prayers on specific days to commit to.
home.step3Body: Volunteers receive daily reminders with their prayer instructions. The organizer can post updates and see the prayer wall fill up.
home.featuresBody: Rooted in Catholic prayer tradition with a curated library of novenas, rosaries, chaplets, litanies, and more.
home.feature1Body: Novenas, rosaries, chaplets, litanies, short prayers, and scripture passages — all with full instructions.
home.feature2Body: See at a glance which days are covered and which need prayer warriors. Novena blocks span 9 days as connected units.
home.feature3Body: Select a situation and we suggest the most appropriate prayers. Illness? Try the Novena to the Sacred Heart. Finances? St. Joseph has you covered.
home.feature4Body: Volunteers can claim prayer slots with just their name and email — no account required. Share one link and watch the calendar fill up.
home.feature5Body: Prayer warriors receive email reminders on their committed days with the full prayer text and instructions.
home.feature6Body: Friends and family can leave messages of encouragement and spiritual support on the prayer train's guestbook.
home.storyParagraph1: We're a faithful Catholic extended family in Massachusetts. In late 2025 and early 2026, three children across our family faced life-threatening crises: a premature baby who spent 73 days in the NICU, a newborn needing open heart surgery in her first week, and a child with a severe respiratory crisis requiring intubation.
home.storyParagraph2: Through the grace of God, the care of Boston Children's Hospital, and the village of aunties, uncles, grandmas, and papas who never left our sides, our children came through. All three. We also know that's not how every story ends. We built PrayerTrain for both: for the road that turns toward life on earth, and the road that turns toward life eternal.
home.finalCTABody: Whether it's a friend battling illness, a family in crisis, or someone discerning their vocation, rally your community to pray with purpose and consistency.

situations.indexDescription: Catholic prayers and ways to organize community prayer when someone you love is facing illness, surgery, grief, or other hard moments.
situations.indexLead: When someone you love is in a hard moment, the question is not usually whether to pray. It is what to pray. Each page below collects the prayers Catholic tradition has given us for one specific situation, with a way to gather others and pray together if you want to.
situations.ctaBody: Start a PrayerTrain anyway. The prayer library covers many more situations than the cluster here, and the create flow will recommend prayers based on the situation you describe.

create.chooseHeading: How can we help you organize prayer?
create.chooseBody: Choose the format that fits how your community wants to pray.
create.calendarBody: A roster of different people each praying something on different days. The “meal train, but for prayers” pattern. You pick a duration, a number of slots per day, and your community fills the calendar.
create.calendarBullet3: Each volunteer commits to one slot, one day
create.calendarExample: Example: a parish coordinating 30 days of prayer for a family in crisis.
create.novenaBody: A small group all praying the same prayer at the same time, every day. The “I'm doing this novena, want to join me?” pattern. You pick a novena from the library, invite friends, and everyone gets the same daily reminder.
create.novenaBullet1: Best for traditional novenas (9 days, 33 days)
create.novenaBullet2: Same prayer every day, in solidarity
create.novenaBullet3: Each member prays every day for the duration
create.novenaExample: Example: starting a St. Blaise novena for a loved one's healing and inviting family to pray it with you.

create.notSureBrowse: see what other people are organizing right now
